questions.stem: The Cartesian equation of plane through $A(7, 8, 6)$ and parallel to the XY plane is
questions.solution:
Step 1: A plane parallel to the XY plane has equation $z = k$ (its normal is along $\hat{k}$).
Step 2: It passes through $A(7, 8, 6)$, so $k = 6$.
Final Answer: (C) $z = 6$
Quick Tip: Parallel to XY plane means only the z-coordinate of the point matters.

questions.stem: The number of ways, in which 6 boys and 5 girls can sit at a round table, if no two girls are to sit together, is
questions.solution:
Step 1: First seat the 6 boys around the round table: $(6-1)! = 5! = 120$ ways.
Step 2: This creates 6 gaps between the boys. Choose and arrange 5 girls in these 6 gaps: ${}^{6}P_{5} = 720$ ways.
Step 3: Total $= 120 \times 720 = 86400$.
Final Answer: (C) 86400
Quick Tip: For 'no two together' on a circle, arrange the others first; $n$ people on a circle leave exactly $n$ gaps.

questions.stem: If $[2\bar{p} - 3\bar{r}\ \ \bar{q}\ \ \bar{s}] + [3\bar{p} + 2\bar{q}\ \ \bar{r}\ \ \bar{s}] = m[\bar{p}\ \ \bar{r}\ \ \bar{s}] + n[\bar{q}\ \ \bar{r}\ \ \bar{s}] + t[\bar{p}\ \ \bar{q}\ \ \bar{s}]$, then the values of $m, n, t$ respectively are ....
questions.solution:
Step 1: Expand using linearity of the scalar triple product: $[2\bar{p} - 3\bar{r}\ \bar{q}\ \bar{s}] = 2[\bar{p}\ \bar{q}\ \bar{s}] - 3[\bar{r}\ \bar{q}\ \bar{s}] = 2[\bar{p}\ \bar{q}\ \bar{s}] + 3[\bar{q}\ \bar{r}\ \bar{s}]$ (swapping two vectors changes the sign).
Step 2: $[3\bar{p} + 2\bar{q}\ \bar{r}\ \bar{s}] = 3[\bar{p}\ \bar{r}\ \bar{s}] + 2[\bar{q}\ \bar{r}\ \bar{s}]$.
Step 3: Sum $= 3[\bar{p}\ \bar{r}\ \bar{s}] + 5[\bar{q}\ \bar{r}\ \bar{s}] + 2[\bar{p}\ \bar{q}\ \bar{s}]$, so $m = 3, n = 5, t = 2$.
Final Answer: (D) $3, 5, 2$
Quick Tip: $[\bar{r}\ \bar{q}\ \bar{s}] = -[\bar{q}\ \bar{r}\ \bar{s}]$; watch the sign when two vectors are interchanged.

questions.stem: The distance of the point $(-3, 2, 3)$ from the line passing through $(4, 6, -2)$ and having direction ratios $-1, 2, 3$ is units.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Let $P(-3, 2, 3)$, $A(4, 6, -2)$, $\bar{b} = (-1, 2, 3)$. Then $\overline{AP} = (-7, -4, 5)$ and $|\bar{b}| = \sqrt{14}$.
Step 2: $\overline{AP} \times \bar{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ -7 & -4 & 5 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = -22\hat{i} + 16\hat{j} - 18\hat{k}$.
Step 3: $|\overline{AP} \times \bar{b}|^{2} = 484 + 256 + 324 = 1064$.
Step 4: $d = \frac{|\overline{AP} \times \bar{b}|}{|\bar{b}|} = \sqrt{\frac{1064}{14}} = \sqrt{76} = 2\sqrt{19}$.
Final Answer: (C) $2\sqrt{19}$
Quick Tip: Distance of a point from a line $= \frac{|\overline{AP} \times \bar{b}|}{|\bar{b}|}$.

questions.stem: A plane passes through $(1, -2, 1)$ and is perpendicular to the planes $2x - 2y + z = 0$ and $x - y + 2z = 4$. The distance of the point $(1, 2, 2)$ from this plane is _______ units.
questions.solution:
Step 1: The normal of the required plane is perpendicular to both normals: $(2, -2, 1) \times (1, -1, 2) = (-4 + 1)\hat{i} - (4 - 1)\hat{j} + (-2 + 2)\hat{k} = (-3, -3, 0)$, i.e. along $(1, 1, 0)$.
Step 2: Plane through $(1, -2, 1)$: $(x - 1) + (y + 2) = 0 \Rightarrow x + y + 1 = 0$.
Step 3: Distance of $(1, 2, 2)$: $\frac{|1 + 2 + 1|}{\sqrt{1 + 1}} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{2}} = 2\sqrt{2}$.
Final Answer: (C) $2\sqrt{2}$
Quick Tip: A plane perpendicular to two planes has normal = cross product of their normals.

questions.stem: The point of intersection of the diagonals of the rectangle whose sides are contained in the lines $x = 8, x = 10, y = 11$ and $y = 12$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: The vertices are $(8, 11), (10, 11), (10, 12), (8, 12)$.
Step 2: The diagonals bisect each other, so they meet at the midpoint of $(8, 11)$ and $(10, 12)$: $\left(\frac{8 + 10}{2}, \frac{11 + 12}{2}\right) = \left(9, \frac{23}{2}\right)$.
Final Answer: (B) $\left(9, \frac{23}{2}\right)$
Quick Tip: The centre of such a rectangle is (mean of the two x-lines, mean of the two y-lines).

questions.stem: A box contains 9 tickets numbered 1 to 9 both inclusive. If 3 tickets are drawn from the box one at a time, then the probability that they are alternatively either {odd, even, odd} or {even, odd, even} is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Odd tickets: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (5); even tickets: 2, 4, 6, 8 (4). Draws are without replacement.
Step 2: $P(\text{odd, even, odd}) = \frac{5}{9} \cdot \frac{4}{8} \cdot \frac{4}{7} = \frac{80}{504}$.
Step 3: $P(\text{even, odd, even}) = \frac{4}{9} \cdot \frac{5}{8} \cdot \frac{3}{7} = \frac{60}{504}$.
Step 4: Required probability $= \frac{80 + 60}{504} = \frac{140}{504} = \frac{5}{18}$.
Final Answer: (D) $\frac{5}{18}$
Quick Tip: 'One at a time' without mention of replacement means without replacement; reduce the total each draw.

Step 1: Let $f(x) = (84 - x)^{1/4}$; then $f(3) = 81^{1/4} = 3$, so the limit is $f'(3)$.
Step 2: $f'(x) = -\frac{1}{4}(84 - x)^{-3/4}$.
Step 3: $f'(3) = -\frac{1}{4} \cdot 81^{-3/4} = -\frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{1}{27} = -\frac{1}{108}$.
Final Answer: (A) $\frac{-1}{108}$
Quick Tip: A limit of the form $\frac{f(x) - f(a)}{x - a}$ is just $f'(a)$.

questions.stem: The statement pattern $[(p \to q) \wedge \sim q] \to r$ is a tautology when $r$ is equivalent to
questions.solution:
Step 1: $(p \to q) \wedge \sim q \equiv (\sim p \vee q) \wedge \sim q \equiv \sim p \wedge \sim q$.
Step 2: The implication $(\sim p \wedge \sim q) \to r$ is a tautology only if $r$ is true whenever $p$ and $q$ are both false.
Step 3: With $p = F, q = F$: $p \wedge \sim q = F$, $q \vee p = F$, $p \wedge q = F$, $\sim q = T$. Only $\sim q$ works (and $\sim p \wedge \sim q \to \sim q$ is always true).
Final Answer: (D) $\sim q$
Quick Tip: An implication fails only for T $\to$ F; check the case where the antecedent is true.

questions.stem: If $3\sin\alpha = 5\sin\beta$, then $\frac{\tan\left(\frac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\right)}{\tan\left(\frac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\right)} =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\frac{\sin\alpha}{\sin\beta} = \frac{5}{3}$. Apply componendo-dividendo: $\frac{\sin\alpha + \sin\beta}{\sin\alpha - \sin\beta} = \frac{5 + 3}{5 - 3} = 4$.
Step 2: $\frac{\sin\alpha + \sin\beta}{\sin\alpha - \sin\beta} = \frac{2\sin\frac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha - \beta}{2}}{2\cos\frac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\sin\frac{\alpha - \beta}{2}} = \frac{\tan\frac{\alpha + \beta}{2}}{\tan\frac{\alpha - \beta}{2}}$.
Step 3: Hence the required ratio is 4.
Final Answer: (D) 4
Quick Tip: Ratio of sines + componendo-dividendo gives the tan-half-sum over tan-half-difference directly.

Step 1: Put $t = e^{x}$, $dx = \frac{dt}{t}$: $I = \int \frac{dt}{t(2t + 1)(t + 1)}$.
Step 2: Partial fractions: $\frac{1}{t(2t + 1)(t + 1)} = \frac{1}{t} - \frac{4}{2t + 1} + \frac{1}{t + 1}$ (put $t = 0, -\frac{1}{2}, -1$).
Step 3: $I = \log t - 2\log(2t + 1) + \log(t + 1) + c = x + \log(e^{x} + 1) - 2\log(2e^{x} + 1) + c$.
Final Answer: (A) $x + \log(e^{x} + 1) - 2\log(2e^{x} + 1) + c$
Quick Tip: $\int \frac{4}{2t + 1}dt = 2\log(2t + 1)$; do not forget to divide by the coefficient of $t$.

questions.stem: $\int \frac{e^{2030\log x} - e^{2029\log x}}{e^{2028\log x} - e^{2027\log x}}\,dx = \ldots$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $e^{k\log x} = x^{k}$, so the integrand is $\frac{x^{2030} - x^{2029}}{x^{2028} - x^{2027}}$.
Step 2: $= \frac{x^{2029}(x - 1)}{x^{2027}(x - 1)} = x^{2}$.
Step 3: $\int x^{2}\,dx = \frac{x^{3}}{3} + c$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{x^{3}}{3} + c$
Quick Tip: Always simplify $e^{k\log x} = x^{k}$ before integrating.

questions.stem: The value of $\int_{1}^{4} \log[x]\,dx$, where $[x]$ is the greatest integer function less than or equal to $x$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Step 1: Split at integers: $\int_{1}^{4} \log[x]\,dx = \int_{1}^{2} \log 1\,dx + \int_{2}^{3} \log 2\,dx + \int_{3}^{4} \log 3\,dx$.
Step 2: $= 0 + \log 2 + \log 3 = \log 6$.
Final Answer: (B) $\log 6$
Quick Tip: For $[x]$ integrals, break the interval at every integer where $[x]$ jumps.

questions.stem: The order and degree of differential equation of all tangent lines to the parabola $x^{2} = 4y$ is respectively.
questions.solution:
Step 1: For $x^{2} = 4ay$ with $a = 1$, a tangent with slope $m$ is $y = mx - m^{2}$ (one arbitrary constant).
Step 2: Differentiate: $\frac{dy}{dx} = m$. Substitute: $y = x\frac{dy}{dx} - \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2}$.
Step 3: Highest derivative is first order, raised to power 2, so order 1, degree 2.
Final Answer: (A) $1, 2$
Quick Tip: Tangent of $x^{2} = 4ay$: $y = mx - am^{2}$; one parameter gives a first-order equation.

questions.stem:
The probability distribution of a discrete random variable X is
X | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4
$P(X = x)$ | 2k | k | 2k | 4k | k
If $a = P(x < 3)$ and $b = P(2 \le X < 4)$, then
questions.solution:
Step 1: Total probability: $2k + k + 2k + 4k + k = 10k = 1 \Rightarrow k = 0.1$.
Step 2: $a = P(X < 3) = 2k + k + 2k = 5k = 0.5$.
Step 3: $b = P(2 \le X < 4) = P(2) + P(3) = 2k + 4k = 6k = 0.6$.
Step 4: So $a < b$.
Final Answer: (C) $a < b$
Quick Tip: Always find $k$ from $\sum P = 1$ first.

questions.stem: If a random variable $X$ has the p.d.f. $f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{k}{x^{2} + 1}, & \text{if } 0 < x < \infty \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$ then c.d.f. of X is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{k}{x^{2} + 1}dx = k\left[\tan^{-1}x\right]_{0}^{\infty} = \frac{k\pi}{2} = 1 \Rightarrow k = \frac{2}{\pi}$.
Step 2: For $x > 0$: $F(x) = \int_{0}^{x} \frac{2}{\pi}\cdot\frac{dt}{1 + t^{2}} = \frac{2}{\pi}\tan^{-1}x$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{2}{\pi}\tan^{-1}x$
Quick Tip: A valid c.d.f. must tend to 1 as $x \to \infty$; only $\frac{2}{\pi}\tan^{-1}x$ does.

questions.stem: If $y = y(x)$ satisfies $\left(\frac{2 + \sin x}{1 + y}\right)\frac{dy}{dx} = -\cos x$ such that $y(0) = 2$, then $y\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Step 1: Separate variables: $\frac{dy}{1 + y} = -\frac{\cos x}{2 + \sin x}dx$.
Step 2: Integrate: $\log(1 + y) = -\log(2 + \sin x) + C \Rightarrow (1 + y)(2 + \sin x) = K$.
Step 3: At $x = 0, y = 2$: $K = 3 \times 2 = 6$.
Step 4: At $x = \frac{\pi}{2}$: $(1 + y)(2 + 1) = 6 \Rightarrow y = 1$.
Final Answer: (D) 1
Quick Tip: $\int \frac{\cos x}{2 + \sin x}dx = \log(2 + \sin x)$ since the numerator is the derivative of the denominator.

questions.stem: In a bank, the principal increases continuously at a rate of $x\%$ per year. Then the rate $x$, if ₹100 double itself in 10 years, is ( $\log 2 = 0.6931$)
questions.solution:
Step 1: Continuous growth: $\frac{dP}{dt} = \frac{x}{100}P \Rightarrow P = P_{0}e^{\frac{xt}{100}}$.
Step 2: Doubling in 10 years: $2 = e^{\frac{10x}{100}} \Rightarrow \frac{x}{10} = \log 2$.
Step 3: $x = 10 \times 0.6931 = 6.931 \approx 6.93$.
Final Answer: (A) $6.93\%$
Quick Tip: Doubling time $T$ at continuous rate $r$: $rT = \log 2$.

questions.stem: If a random variable $X$ follows the Binomial distribution $B(33, p)$ such that $3P(X = 0) = P(X = 1)$, then the variance of X is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $3q^{33} = {}^{33}C_{1}\,p\,q^{32} \Rightarrow 3q = 33p \Rightarrow q = 11p$.
Step 2: $p + q = 1 \Rightarrow 12p = 1 \Rightarrow p = \frac{1}{12}, q = \frac{11}{12}$.
Step 3: Variance $= npq = 33 \cdot \frac{1}{12} \cdot \frac{11}{12} = \frac{363}{144} = \frac{121}{48}$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{121}{48}$
Quick Tip: For binomial, variance $= npq$; reduce $\frac{363}{144}$ by 3.

questions.stem: The number of common tangents that can be drawn to the circles $x^{2} + y^{2} - 6x = 0$ and $x^{2} + y^{2} + 6x + 2y + 1 = 0$ is ________
questions.solution:
Step 1: Circle 1: centre $C_{1}(3, 0)$, $r_{1} = 3$. Circle 2: centre $C_{2}(-3, -1)$, $r_{2} = \sqrt{9 + 1 - 1} = 3$.
Step 2: $C_{1}C_{2} = \sqrt{36 + 1} = \sqrt{37} \approx 6.08$.
Step 3: $C_{1}C_{2} > r_{1} + r_{2} = 6$, so the circles are separate and have 4 common tangents.
Final Answer: (D) 4
Quick Tip: $d > r_{1} + r_{2}$: 4; $d = r_{1} + r_{2}$: 3; intersecting: 2; touching internally: 1; one inside other: 0.

questions.stem:
The sum to infinite terms of the series
$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{9}\right) + \ldots\ldots\ldots + \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2^{n-1}}{1 + 2^{2n-1}}\right) + \ldots\ldots$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Write $\frac{2^{n-1}}{1 + 2^{2n-1}} = \frac{2^{n} - 2^{n-1}}{1 + 2^{n}\cdot 2^{n-1}}$, so $T_{n} = \tan^{-1}2^{n} - \tan^{-1}2^{n-1}$.
Step 2: The sum telescopes: $S_{n} = \tan^{-1}2^{n} - \tan^{-1}1$.
Step 3: As $n \to \infty$, $\tan^{-1}2^{n} \to \frac{\pi}{2}$, so $S = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{4}$.
Final Answer: (A) $\frac{\pi}{4}$
Quick Tip: Split $\frac{x - y}{1 + xy}$ to get a telescoping difference of $\tan^{-1}$ terms.

questions.stem: The ratios of sides in a triangle ABC are $5 : 12 : 13$ and its area is 270 . Then sides of the triangle are
questions.solution:
Step 1: Let sides be $5k, 12k, 13k$. Since $(5k)^{2} + (12k)^{2} = (13k)^{2}$, the triangle is right-angled.
Step 2: Area $= \frac{1}{2}(5k)(12k) = 30k^{2} = 270 \Rightarrow k^{2} = 9 \Rightarrow k = 3$.
Step 3: Sides are $15, 36, 39$.
Final Answer: (C) $15, 36, 39$
Quick Tip: Spot the Pythagorean triple 5-12-13 to use the simple right-triangle area.

questions.stem: If $4\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x = \pi$ then $x =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Use $\cos^{-1}x = \frac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1}x$: $4\sin^{-1}x + \frac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1}x = \pi$.
Step 2: $3\sin^{-1}x = \frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow \sin^{-1}x = \frac{\pi}{6}$.
Step 3: $x = \sin\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{1}{2}$
Quick Tip: $\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x = \frac{\pi}{2}$ converts mixed equations to one function.

questions.stem: $\int_{1}^{e} \frac{e^{x}}{x}(1 + x\log x)\,dx =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Integrand $= e^{x}\left(\frac{1}{x} + \log x\right) = e^{x}\left(f(x) + f'(x)\right)$ with $f(x) = \log x$.
Step 2: $\int e^{x}(f + f')\,dx = e^{x}f(x)$, so $I = \left[e^{x}\log x\right]_{1}^{e}$.
Step 3: $I = e^{e}\cdot 1 - e\cdot 0 = e^{e}$.
Final Answer: (A) $e^{e}$
Quick Tip: Look for the pattern $e^{x}[f(x) + f'(x)]$.

questions.stem: The ratio of the areas bounded by the curves $y = \cos x$ and $y = \cos 2x$ between $x = 0, x = \frac{\pi}{3}$ and X -axis is
The solution of the differential equation $x\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = 1$ at $x = y = 1$ with $\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$ at $x = 1$, is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \frac{1}{x} \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = \log x + c_{1}$. Using $\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$ at $x = 1$: $c_{1} = 0$.
Step 2: $y = \int \log x\,dx = x\log x - x + c_{2}$.
Step 3: At $x = 1, y = 1$: $1 = 0 - 1 + c_{2} \Rightarrow c_{2} = 2$. So $y = x\log x - x + 2$.
Final Answer: (B) $y = x\log x - x + 2$
Quick Tip: $\int \log x\,dx = x\log x - x$; use each condition right after the integration it fixes.

questions.stem: The volume of the tetrahedron whose co-terminus edges are $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ is 12 cubic units. If the scalar projection of $\bar{a}$ on $\bar{b} \times \bar{c}$ is 4 , then $|\bar{b} \times \bar{c}| =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Volume of tetrahedron $= \frac{1}{6}|[\bar{a}\ \bar{b}\ \bar{c}]| = 12 \Rightarrow [\bar{a}\ \bar{b}\ \bar{c}] = 72$.
Step 2: Scalar projection of $\bar{a}$ on $\bar{b} \times \bar{c}$ $= \frac{\bar{a}\cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})}{|\bar{b} \times \bar{c}|} = \frac{72}{|\bar{b} \times \bar{c}|} = 4$.
Step 3: $|\bar{b} \times \bar{c}| = \frac{72}{4} = 18$.
Final Answer: (A) 18
Quick Tip: Tetrahedron volume is $\frac{1}{6}$ of the box product, not $\frac{1}{3}$.

questions.stem: If the sum of the squares of the distance of the point $P(x, y, z)$ from the co-ordinate axes is 242 , then the distance of the point P from the origin is units.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Squared distances from the X, Y, Z axes are $y^{2} + z^{2}$, $z^{2} + x^{2}$, $x^{2} + y^{2}$.
Step 2: Sum $= 2(x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}) = 242 \Rightarrow x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 121$.
Step 3: $OP = \sqrt{121} = 11$.
Final Answer: (B) 11
Quick Tip: Distance from the X-axis is $\sqrt{y^{2} + z^{2}}$ (drop the coordinate of that axis).

questions.stem: If the points $A(2 - x, 2, 2), B(2, 2 - y, 2), C(2, 2, 2 - z)$ and $D(1, 1, 1)$ are coplanar, then the locus of point $P(x, y, z)$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\overline{DA} = (1 - x, 1, 1)$, $\overline{DB} = (1, 1 - y, 1)$, $\overline{DC} = (1, 1, 1 - z)$. Coplanar $\Rightarrow [\overline{DA}\ \overline{DB}\ \overline{DC}] = 0$.
Step 2: $\begin{vmatrix} 1 - x & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 - y & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 - z \end{vmatrix} = (1 - x)[(1 - y)(1 - z) - 1] - [(1 - z) - 1] + [1 - (1 - y)] = xy + yz + zx - xyz$.
Step 3: $xy + yz + zx = xyz$; dividing by $xyz$: $\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{z} = 1$.
Final Answer: (A) $\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{z} = 1$
Quick Tip: Four points are coplanar when the box product of three vectors from one of them is zero.

questions.stem: If the lines $\frac{3 - x}{2} = \frac{5y - 2}{3\lambda + 1} = 5 - z$ and $\frac{x + 2}{-1} = \frac{1 - 3y}{7} = \frac{4 - z}{2\mu}$ are at right angles, then $7\lambda - 10\mu =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Line 1 in standard form: $\frac{x - 3}{-2} = \frac{y - \frac{2}{5}}{\frac{3\lambda + 1}{5}} = \frac{z - 5}{-1}$; d.r. $\left(-2, \frac{3\lambda + 1}{5}, -1\right)$.
Step 2: Line 2: $\frac{x + 2}{-1} = \frac{y - \frac{1}{3}}{-\frac{7}{3}} = \frac{z - 4}{-2\mu}$; d.r. $\left(-1, -\frac{7}{3}, -2\mu\right)$.
Step 3: Perpendicular: $2 - \frac{7(3\lambda + 1)}{15} + 2\mu = 0 \Rightarrow 30 - 21\lambda - 7 + 30\mu = 0 \Rightarrow 21\lambda - 30\mu = 23$.
Step 4: Dividing by 3: $7\lambda - 10\mu = \frac{23}{3}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\frac{23}{3}$
Quick Tip: Make the coefficients of $x, y, z$ equal to $+1$ before reading direction ratios.

questions.stem: If the angle $\theta$ between the line $\frac{x + 1}{1} = \frac{y - 1}{2} = \frac{z - 2}{2}$ and the plane $2x - y + \sqrt{\lambda}z + 4 = 0$ is such that $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{3}$, then $\lambda + 1 =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Line direction $\bar{b} = (1, 2, 2)$, $|\bar{b}| = 3$; plane normal $\bar{n} = (2, -1, \sqrt{\lambda})$, $|\bar{n}| = \sqrt{5 + \lambda}$.
Step 2: $\sin\theta = \frac{|\bar{b}\cdot\bar{n}|}{|\bar{b}||\bar{n}|} = \frac{|2 - 2 + 2\sqrt{\lambda}|}{3\sqrt{5 + \lambda}} = \frac{1}{3}$.
Step 3: $2\sqrt{\lambda} = \sqrt{5 + \lambda} \Rightarrow 4\lambda = 5 + \lambda \Rightarrow \lambda = \frac{5}{3}$.
Step 4: $\lambda + 1 = \frac{8}{3}$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{8}{3}$
Quick Tip: Line-plane angle uses $\sin\theta$ (not $\cos\theta$) with the plane's normal.

questions.stem: The feasible region represented by the given constraints $2x + 3y \ge 12, -x + y \le 3, x \le 4, y \ge 3$ is denoted by
questions.solution:
Step 1: $y \ge 3$ keeps the region above the line $y = 3$, which rules out $S_{2}$ and $S_{3}$.
Step 2: $-x + y \le 3$ (test origin: $0 \le 3$ true) keeps the side of $-x + y = 3$ towards the origin, i.e. to its right; $x \le 4$ keeps it left of $x = 4$.
Step 3: $2x + 3y \ge 12$ (origin gives $0 \ge 12$, false) keeps the side away from the origin. The region above $y = 3$, right of $-x + y = 3$ and beyond $2x + 3y = 12$ is $S_{1}$.
Final Answer: (A) $S_{1}$
Quick Tip: Test the origin in each inequality to pick the correct side of each line.

questions.stem: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ if $y = ax^{n+1} + bx^{-n}$, then $x^{2}\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\frac{dy}{dx} = a(n + 1)x^{n} - bnx^{-n-1}$.
Step 2: $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = a n(n + 1)x^{n-1} + bn(n + 1)x^{-n-2}$.
Step 3: $x^{2}\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = n(n + 1)\left(ax^{n+1} + bx^{-n}\right) = n(n + 1)y$.
Final Answer: (C) $n(n + 1)y$
Quick Tip: $(-n)(-n - 1) = n(n + 1)$, the same factor as for $x^{n+1}$.

questions.stem:
$f(x) = (\cos x + i\sin x)\cdot(\cos 3x + i\sin 3x)\cdots[\cos(2n - 1)x + i\sin(2n - 1)x]\ n \in \mathbb{N}$
Then $f''(x) =$ ______ , (Where $i = \sqrt{-1}$ )
questions.solution:
Step 1: By De Moivre, the product is $\cos(Sx) + i\sin(Sx) = e^{iSx}$ with $S = 1 + 3 + \ldots + (2n - 1) = n^{2}$.
Step 2: $f(x) = e^{in^{2}x} \Rightarrow f'(x) = in^{2}f(x)$.
Step 3: $f''(x) = (in^{2})^{2}f(x) = -n^{4}f(x)$.
Final Answer: (B) $-n^{4}f(x)$
Quick Tip: Sum of the first $n$ odd numbers is $n^{2}$.

questions.stem: A population $p(t)$ of 1000 bacteria introduced into a nutrient medium grows according to the relation $p(t) = 1000 + \frac{1000t}{100 + t^{2}}$. The maximum size of this bacterial population is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $p'(t) = \frac{1000(100 + t^{2}) - 1000t(2t)}{(100 + t^{2})^{2}} = \frac{1000(100 - t^{2})}{(100 + t^{2})^{2}}$.
Step 2: $p'(t) = 0 \Rightarrow t = 10$ ($t > 0$); $p'$ changes from + to -, so it is a maximum.
Step 3: $p(10) = 1000 + \frac{10000}{200} = 1050$.
Final Answer: (C) 1050
Quick Tip: $\frac{t}{100 + t^{2}}$ is maximum at $t = \sqrt{100}$ (AM-GM).

questions.stem: An ellipse has OB as semi-minor axis, S and $S'$ are foci and angle SBS' is a right angle. Then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $B(0, b)$, $S(ae, 0)$, $S'(-ae, 0)$. $\angle SBS' = 90^\circ$ means slopes of $BS$ and $BS'$ multiply to $-1$: $\left(-\frac{b}{ae}\right)\left(\frac{b}{ae}\right) = -1 \Rightarrow b^{2} = a^{2}e^{2}$.
Step 2: Also $b^{2} = a^{2}(1 - e^{2})$, so $e^{2} = 1 - e^{2} \Rightarrow e^{2} = \frac{1}{2}$.
Step 3: $e = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
Quick Tip: Eccentricity of an ellipse is always less than 1, so $\sqrt{2}$ is impossible.

questions.stem: If the directed line makes an angle $45^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ with the X and Y -axes respectively, then the obtuse angle $\theta$ made by the line with the Z -axis is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\cos^{2}45^\circ + \cos^{2}60^\circ + \cos^{2}\theta = 1 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} + \cos^{2}\theta = 1$.
Step 2: $\cos^{2}\theta = \frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow \cos\theta = -\frac{1}{2}$ (obtuse).
Step 3: $\theta = 120^\circ$.
Final Answer: (B) $120^\circ$
Quick Tip: Sum of squares of direction cosines is 1; obtuse angle means negative cosine.

questions.stem: The derivative of $\tan^{-1}\left(\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} - 1\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Let $u = \sqrt{1 + x^{2}} - 1$; $\frac{du}{dx} = \frac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}}$.
Step 2: $1 + u^{2} = 1 + (1 + x^{2}) - 2\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} + 1 = x^{2} - 2\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} + 3$.
Step 3: $\frac{d}{dx}\tan^{-1}u = \frac{u'}{1 + u^{2}} = \frac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}\left(x^{2} - 2\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} + 3\right)}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\frac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}\left(x^{2} - 2\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} + 3\right)}$
Quick Tip: Expand $(\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} - 1)^{2}$ carefully: the constant terms give $1 + 1 + 1 = 3$.

questions.stem: By dropping a stone in a quiet lake, a wave in the form of circle is generated. The radius of the circular wave increases at the rate of $2.1\ \mathrm{cm/sec}$. Then the rate of increase of the enclosed circular region, when the radius of the circular wave is 10 cm , is (Given $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution:
Step 1: Area $A = \pi r^{2} \Rightarrow \frac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r\frac{dr}{dt}$.
Step 2: $\frac{dA}{dt} = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 10 \times 2.1 = 2 \times 22 \times 10 \times 0.3 = 132$.
Final Answer: (C) $132\ \mathrm{cm^{2}}$/ second
Quick Tip: $\frac{2.1}{7} = 0.3$ makes the arithmetic quick.

questions.stem: The angle between the curves $xy = 6$ and $x^{2}y = 12$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Intersection: dividing, $x = \frac{12}{6} = 2$, then $y = 3$. Point $(2, 3)$.
Step 2: $y = \frac{6}{x} \Rightarrow m_{1} = -\frac{6}{x^{2}} = -\frac{3}{2}$; $y = \frac{12}{x^{2}} \Rightarrow m_{2} = -\frac{24}{x^{3}} = -3$.
Step 3: $\tan\theta = \left|\frac{m_{1} - m_{2}}{1 + m_{1}m_{2}}\right| = \frac{\frac{3}{2}}{1 + \frac{9}{2}} = \frac{3}{11}$.
Final Answer: (A) $\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{11}$
Quick Tip: Angle between curves = angle between their tangents at the point of intersection.

questions.stem: In the mean value theorem, $f'(c) = \frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$, if $a = 0$, $b = \frac{1}{2}$ and $f(x) = x(x - 1)(x - 2)$, then the value of $c$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $f(x) = x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 2x$; $f(0) = 0$, $f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\cdot\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = \frac{3}{8}$.
Step 2: $\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a} = \frac{3/8}{1/2} = \frac{3}{4}$.
Step 3: $f'(c) = 3c^{2} - 6c + 2 = \frac{3}{4} \Rightarrow 12c^{2} - 24c + 5 = 0 \Rightarrow c = \frac{24 \pm \sqrt{576 - 240}}{24} = 1 \pm \frac{\sqrt{21}}{6}$.
Step 4: $c$ must lie in $\left(0, \frac{1}{2}\right)$: $1 - \frac{\sqrt{21}}{6} \approx 0.236$ works.
Final Answer: (C) $1 - \frac{\sqrt{21}}{6}$
Quick Tip: Reject the root outside $(a, b)$.

questions.stem: $\int \frac{\sin 2x}{(a + b\cos x)^{2}}dx =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x$. Put $t = a + b\cos x$: $dt = -b\sin x\,dx$, $\cos x = \frac{t - a}{b}$.
Step 2: $I = \int \frac{2\cdot\frac{t - a}{b}}{t^{2}}\cdot\left(-\frac{dt}{b}\right) = -\frac{2}{b^{2}}\int\left(\frac{1}{t} - \frac{a}{t^{2}}\right)dt$.
Step 3: $I = -\frac{2}{b^{2}}\left[\log t + \frac{a}{t}\right] + c = \frac{-2}{b^{2}}\left[\log(a + b\cos x) + \frac{a}{a + b\cos x}\right] + c$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{-2}{b^{2}}\left[\log(a + b\cos x) + \frac{a}{a + b\cos x}\right] + c$
Quick Tip: $\int -\frac{a}{t^{2}}dt = +\frac{a}{t}$; track this sign carefully.

questions.stem: If $m_{1}$ and $m_{2}$ are the slopes of the lines represented by $ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0$ satisfying the condition $16h^{2} = 25ab$, then ............ .
questions.solution:
Step 1: $m_{1} + m_{2} = -\frac{2h}{b}$, $m_{1}m_{2} = \frac{a}{b}$.
Step 2: Test $m_{1} = 4m_{2}$: $5m_{2} = -\frac{2h}{b} \Rightarrow m_{2} = -\frac{2h}{5b}$, and $4m_{2}^{2} = \frac{a}{b}$.
Step 3: $4\cdot\frac{4h^{2}}{25b^{2}} = \frac{a}{b} \Rightarrow 16h^{2} = 25ab$, which is the given condition.
Final Answer: (B) $m_{1} = 4m_{2}$
Quick Tip: If $m_{1} = km_{2}$, then $4kh^{2} = (1 + k)^{2}ab$; with $k = 4$ this is $16h^{2} = 25ab$.

questions.stem: The modulus of the square root of the conjugate of $-7 + 24\sqrt{-1}$ is ________
questions.solution:
Step 1: Conjugate $\bar{z} = -7 - 24i$; $|\bar{z}| = \sqrt{49 + 576} = 25$.
Step 2: $|\sqrt{\bar{z}}| = \sqrt{|\bar{z}|} = \sqrt{25} = 5$.
Final Answer: (D) 5
Quick Tip: Conjugation does not change modulus, and $|\sqrt{z}| = \sqrt{|z|}$.

Step 1: Write $x = \log_{15}15^{x}$: $\log_{15}\left[15^{x}(5 + 3^{x})\right] = \log_{15}\left[5^{x}\cdot 24\right]$.
Step 2: $15^{x}(5 + 3^{x}) = 24\cdot 5^{x} \Rightarrow 3^{x}(5 + 3^{x}) = 24$.
Step 3: Let $t = 3^{x}$: $t^{2} + 5t - 24 = 0 \Rightarrow (t + 8)(t - 3) = 0 \Rightarrow t = 3$ (as $t > 0$), so $x = 1$.
Final Answer: (A) 1
Quick Tip: Convert the lone $x$ into $\log_{15}15^{x}$ so both sides become a single log.

questions.stem: If $f(x)$ is continuous at point $x = 0$ where $f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{3\sin x + 5\tan x}{a^{x} - 1}, & x < 0 \\ \frac{2}{\log 2}, & x = 0 \\ \frac{8x + 2x\cos x}{b^{x} - 1}, & x > 0 \end{cases}$ then the values of a and b , respectively, are ________
questions.solution:
Step 1: LHL $= \lim_{x \to 0}\frac{3\frac{\sin x}{x} + 5\frac{\tan x}{x}}{\frac{a^{x} - 1}{x}} = \frac{8}{\log a}$. Set $= \frac{2}{\log 2} \Rightarrow \log a = 4\log 2 \Rightarrow a = 16$.
Step 2: RHL $= \lim_{x \to 0}\frac{8 + 2\cos x}{\frac{b^{x} - 1}{x}} = \frac{10}{\log b}$. Set $= \frac{2}{\log 2} \Rightarrow \log b = 5\log 2 \Rightarrow b = 32$.
Final Answer: (B) 16, 32
Quick Tip: $\lim_{x \to 0}\frac{a^{x} - 1}{x} = \log a$.

questions.stem: The smallest angle of the triangle whose sides are $6 + \sqrt{12}, \sqrt{48}, \sqrt{24}$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $a = 6 + 2\sqrt{3} \approx 9.46$, $b = 4\sqrt{3} \approx 6.93$, $c = 2\sqrt{6} \approx 4.90$. The smallest angle $C$ is opposite the smallest side $c$.
Step 2: $a^{2} = 48 + 24\sqrt{3}$, $b^{2} = 48$, $c^{2} = 24$. $\cos C = \frac{a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2}}{2ab} = \frac{72 + 24\sqrt{3}}{8\sqrt{3}(6 + 2\sqrt{3})} = \frac{24(3 + \sqrt{3})}{48(\sqrt{3} + 1)}$.
Step 3: Since $3 + \sqrt{3} = \sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3} + 1)$, $\cos C = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \Rightarrow C = \frac{\pi}{6}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\frac{\pi}{6}$
Quick Tip: The smallest angle is always opposite the smallest side.

questions.stem:
Consider the three statements
p : $\forall n \in \mathbb{N}$, $10n - 3$ is a prime number, when n is not divisible by 3.
q : $\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}, \frac{-2}{\sqrt{3}}, \frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}$ are the direction cosines of a directed line.
r : $\sin x$ is an increasing function in the interval $\left[\frac{-\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$.
Then which of the following statement pattern has truth value true?
questions.solution:
Step 1: p: for $n = 8$ (not divisible by 3), $10n - 3 = 77 = 7 \times 11$, not prime, so p is F.
Step 2: q: $\frac{4}{3} + \frac{4}{3} + \frac{1}{3} = 3 \neq 1$, so q is F. r: $\sin x$ increases on $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$, so r is T.
Step 3: (A) $F \leftrightarrow T = F$; (B) $(F \to F) \to F = T \to F = F$; (C) $(T \vee F) \wedge T = T$; (D) $(T \wedge T) \leftrightarrow F = F$.
Final Answer: (C) $(\sim p \vee q) \wedge r$
Quick Tip: One counterexample ($n = 8$) is enough to make a 'for all' statement false.

questions.stem: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\theta & \sin\theta & 0 \\ -\sin\theta & \cos\theta & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, where $A_{21}, A_{22}, A_{23}$ are cofactors of $a_{21}, a_{22}, a_{23}$ respectively, then the value of $a_{21}A_{21} + a_{22}A_{22} + a_{23}A_{23} =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: The sum of products of elements of a row with their own cofactors equals $|A|$.
Step 2: $|A| = \cos\theta(\cos\theta - 0) - \sin\theta(-\sin\theta - 0) + 0 = \cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta = 1$.
Final Answer: (A) 1
Quick Tip: Own cofactors give $|A|$; cofactors of a different row give 0.

questions.stem: In a triangle $ABC$, with usual notations, if $\frac{b + c}{11} = \frac{c + a}{12} = \frac{a + b}{13}$ Then $\cos A : \cos B : \cos C$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Let $b + c = 11k$, $c + a = 12k$, $a + b = 13k$. Adding: $a + b + c = 18k$, so $a = 7k, b = 6k, c = 5k$.
Step 2: $\cos A = \frac{36 + 25 - 49}{60} = \frac{1}{5}$, $\cos B = \frac{49 + 25 - 36}{70} = \frac{19}{35}$, $\cos C = \frac{49 + 36 - 25}{84} = \frac{5}{7}$.
Step 3: Multiply by 35: $\cos A : \cos B : \cos C = 7 : 19 : 25$.
Final Answer: (A) $7 : 19 : 25$
Quick Tip: Add the three equations to get the semi-sum, then subtract each to get the sides.
